text: Polymorphism means many different objects can respond to the same method call, each in its own way.
Every Shape promises an area method, even though the base class doesn't know how to compute it.
Square implements area as side squared, while Circle uses pi times radius squared.
[chuckle] The magic is here — we put different shapes in one list and treat them identically.
The loop calls dot area on each, and Python automatically runs the right version for that object.
[sniff] The loop doesn't know or care whether it's holding a square or a circle — it just asks for the area.
Each shape answers correctly, using its own formula, from the very same line of code.
[sigh] That's the power — you write general code once, and it works with any object that honors the interface.
[groan] Polymorphism is what makes object-oriented code so extensible — add a new shape, and the loop just works.
